title: Milestone Pulseboard for Compliance Waves: Auto-assign, Drift Detection, and Remediation Runbooks
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: Tracking compliance milestones across SOC2/ISO and SSO/audit-log workstreams is manual and error-prone. Teams miss evidence handoffs, drift in implemented controls goes undetected, and remediation runbooks are scattered across Confluence and PRs.

Goal: Build a Milestone Pulseboard that consolidates compliance milestones into a single lifecycle view with three automation pillars: 1) auto-assignment of evidence tasks to owners based on ownership mappings; 2) continuous drift detection that flags missing evidence or configuration changes (e.g., SSO metadata, audit-log retention) against the expected checklist; 3) integrated remediation runbooks that can be triggered from the board and surface relevant PRs, runbooks, and postmortems.

Deliverables: 
- Pulseboard UI in Console (mockups + prototype) showing milestone lanes, evidence status, ownership, and SLA timers.
- Backend sync job to reconcile Proof-of-Evidence (PoE) attachments from Drive/Confluence and map them to milestone tasks.
- Drift detector service (lightweight) that compares live config/state to milestone checklists and emits issues.
- Runbook templates (SSO, audit-log retention, KMS rotation, incident evidence) and one-click remediation links to GitHub PR templates and Confluence runbooks.
- Pager/alerting hooks for missed milestone SLAs and high-severity drift.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Pulseboard shows status for all active SOC2/ISO milestones with >95% fidelity to our evidence index.
- Auto-assigned tasks are created for 90% of incoming evidence events for the pilot orgs.
- Drift detector catches seeded config changes in staging (tests) and raises the correct severity and suggested runbook within 5 minutes.
- Documentation and runbooks published; security review completed for automated remediation steps.

Out of scope for initial rollout: full RBAC for multi-tenant orgs (phase 2), on-prem agent for evidence collection (phase 3).
